This is a NEW registration designed AFTER seeing all their results, including held-out scores.
why: Two weaknesses named in the gate scoring of 2026-11-14 (PROGRESS/27). (A) In long_prereg_dom3.json the LSTM and GRU read 5 channels over 10 bins while the two published quantum reservoirs read one series, so 'quantum reservoirs are detectably worse than the networks' is not like for like. (B) The mechanism check was mixed: at 15 minutes the two 28-number stand-ins did not reproduce a 0.4 to 0.5% gain of the quantum reservoirs, and those stand-ins were themselves weak there. A 28-number state is much smaller than the quantum reservoir's hidden state.
questions: Q-A: do an LSTM and a GRU that read ONLY the single series of the quantum reservoirs still beat them?
Q-B: does a classical stand-in with a larger hidden state (256 numbers), still read through 28 numbers, match the quantum reservoirs where the small stand-ins did not?

models.read_not_rerun: DOM, ESN28u (long_preds_dom); ISING, ESN28u_t (long_preds_dom2); ESNq_t, SAS28_t, LSTM, GRU (long_preds_dom3); benchmark as before.
models.LSTM1_GRU1_intraday: dom3_lib.fit_seq unchanged (one recurrent layer + linear head, Adam, squared error on the standardised benchmark residual, batch 512, at most 30 epochs, patience 4; 12 configurations hidden {8,16,32} x learning rate {3e-4,1e-3,3e-3,1e-2}; tuning seed 100; seeds 0-9 averaged). The ONLY change from LSTM/GRU: the input is ONE channel, the last 10 bins of ln RV (standardised with training rows) instead of 5 channels.
models.LSTM1_GRU1_daily: dom3_lib.fit_daily unchanged; the input is ONE series, the last 5 days of ln daily range variance (lvR1) instead of the three HAR inputs. The anchor lvR5 is kept (the reservoir readouts also use it).
models.ESNb_t: dom4_lib.esn_big: the ESNq_t design (two inputs u and sqrt(u(1-u)), input scale 0.5) with 256 units, read through 28 fixed random Gaussian projections. Same 12 configurations (spectral radius {0.6,0.9,1.2} x leak {0.1,0.2,0.5,1.0}).
models.SASb_t: dom4_lib.sas_big: the SAS28_t design (state-affine update with coefficients 1-u, u, sqrt(u(1-u)), no tanh) with a 256-number state, read through 28 fixed random Gaussian projections. Same 12 configurations (gain {0.3,0.5,0.65} x leak {0.1,0.2,0.5,1.0}).
models.standin_tuning_and_readout: Exactly as long_prereg_dom3.json (tuning seeds 100, 101 intraday by validation MSE; 100-102 daily by validation QLIKE; then seeds 0-9; same readouts with 28 features).
models.everything_else: Rows, targets, splits, purge, benchmark, input series and scaling exactly as before (dom4_run.py and dom4_daily.py are generated from dom3_run.py and dom3_daily.py with only the model lines changed; the row-building section is identical to dom2_run.py by diff). dom4_report.py stops if rows, targets or benchmark forecasts differ between stored files.

what_is_and_is_not_matched_in_A: Matched: the input series, the benchmark, the rows, the residual target, 10 seeds. Not matched: the networks see a window of 10 bins (5 days on D) while the reservoirs run recurrently over the whole block, which favours the reservoirs on memory length; the networks are trained end to end while the reservoirs train only a linear readout on 28 features, which favours the networks. Family T1 is 'like for like in input', not in model size or training.
blocks: As before: intraday H, M, F test years 2013-2025; daily D test years 2015-2024; held-out intraday 2026 and daily 2025, 2026, run after the rolling report is written.
statistics: As long_prereg_dom3.json (loss, HAC interval, lags, +/-3% band, verdict words, size categories, Holm within family and stratum, regimes). Families: M2 mechanism, larger stand-ins (Holm over 4) = DOM vs ESNb_t, DOM vs SASb_t, ISING vs ESNb_t, ISING vs SASb_t; T1 quantum vs single-input networks (Holm over 4) = DOM, ISING each vs LSTM1 and vs GRU1; L1 single-input networks (Holm over 4) = LSTM1 vs benchmark, GRU1 vs benchmark, LSTM1 vs LSTM, GRU1 vs GRU (the last two measure what the extra four channels add); C descriptive = ESNb_t vs ESNq_t, SASb_t vs SAS28_t (effect of the larger state), ESNb_t vs ESN28u_t, SASb_t vs ESN28u_t, LSTM1 vs ESN28u_t, GRU1 vs ESN28u_t, LSTM1 vs ESNb_t, LSTM1 vs SASb_t.

decision_rules.A_like_for_like: Per grid, pooled: the ordering 'networks above quantum reservoirs' HOLDS like for like if DOM and ISING are both 'detectably worse' than the better of LSTM1 and GRU1 (lower pooled loss). It DOES NOT HOLD if either is 'no detectable difference', 'detectable, below band' or 'meaningful edge'; then the paper says the networks' lead in long_prereg_dom3.json comes at least partly from their extra inputs. A quantum 'meaningful edge' over the single-input networks would be reported as an edge over that model only, not as a quantum advantage.
decision_rules.B_mechanism: Per grid and per quantum reservoir, pooled: 'explained by a larger classical stand-in' if against AT LEAST ONE of ESNb_t, SASb_t the category is 'no detectable difference' or 'detectably worse'; otherwise 'not explained'. Read together with long_prereg_dom3.json.
decision_rules.final_wording_for_the_paper: Fixed now. On a grid where a gain over ESN28u_t existed (M and F): if explained by any of the four stand-ins (this run or the last), the paper says the gain is reproduced by a classical model of the same form; if explained by none, the paper says 'a gain of under 1% that four classical stand-ins of the same form did not reproduce', and states that this is not evidence of a quantum advantage (below the +/-3% band; the simulation is itself classical; other classical models are not excluded).
decision_rules.heldout: Same categories on held-out data, one stratum, read together with the rolling result.

student_prediction.reading: NOT stated. The student answered 'yes register and run A and B'. Left null.

claude_prediction_recorded_for_transpare.text: A: the single-input networks lose most of their lead. LSTM1 and GRU1 beat the benchmark by about 1 to 2% intraday and are within 1% of DOM and ISING; the ordering holds like for like on at most one intraday grid, so most of the 2 to 6% lead in the last run came from the extra channels. B: the larger stand-ins are 0.1 to 0.3% better than the small ones and match DOM at 15 minutes rolling ('explained'); ISING stays 'not explained' at 15 minutes. Daily: no detectable differences. One of my three earlier predictions in this series was partly right, two were wrong.

checks_done_before_registration: Nothing scored. (1) dom4_lib.selftest on random numbers: both larger stand-ins give 28 finite, input-responsive features, forget their start, and the stacked update equals the direct one. (2) dom4_run.py H 2015 with DRY=1: shapes only (network input (rows, 10, 1)); no forecast kept. (3) diff: row-building section identical to dom2_run.py. (4) py_compile of the three scripts; dom4_report.py uses the comparison, Holm and category functions of dom3_report.py unchanged. (5) Timing on random numbers: 22 and 38 microseconds per step for the larger stand-ins. dom4_daily.py and dom4_report.py were NOT executed before registration.
known_limits: Fourth test in a sequence, designed after seeing every earlier result including held-out 2025-26. The held-out period is unseen only for the four new models. This cannot be repaired by more runs on the same data.

Run B adds stand-ins after a mixed result. To limit the freedom this gives, the family (two designs, one size, same grids) and the paper's wording for each outcome are fixed here, and the stop rule forbids further stand-ins.
256 numbers is still smaller than the quantum memory (a 64 x 64 density matrix). 'Not explained' remains weak evidence.
Run A matches the input only (see what_is_and_is_not_matched_in_A). Window length is not tuned.

All earlier limits remain: authors' designs on a different task, details that are my reading of a preprint, min-max scaling, exact simulation, copper only, overlapping blocks, narrow HAC intervals at intraday sample sizes, small network search, no QLSTM on the ladder, AI-written code not re-derived by the student, licensed data not committed.
cost_estimate: From the measured third run (1 h 23 min) plus about 12 minutes of stand-in time per 5-minute block: roughly 1.5 to 2.5 hours. No hardware jobs; no new data.
stop_rule: One run of the registered jobs (39 intraday and 10 daily rolling blocks, then 5 held-out jobs), report and stop. No further stand-ins, network variants, grids, seeds or categories on these data after results. A crashed job is re-run unchanged.
